records.text:
Is your bedtime snack hurting your kidneys? Or helping them?

In this video, a doctor explains the best fruit to eat before bed for healthy kidneys, and which fruits to be careful with.

Your blood pressure is supposed to drop at night. That rest is good for your heart and your kidneys. But salty snacks can get in the way. The right swap can help.

This video is for adults over 60 and the people who love them. About 1 in 3 adults over 65 has kidney disease. Most don't know it.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN
• Why your blood pressure should drop at night
• Why no fruit can cure kidney disease (and what fruit can do)
• Blueberries and other berries: what the research shows
• Apples: the easiest, cheapest choice
• The potassium warning most people never hear
• Cranberries and UTIs: who they may help
• Tart cherries and sleep: what one small study found
• What matters more than the fruit
• A simple 7-night plan to start tonight

4 QUESTIONS TO ASK YOUR DOCTOR
1. What is my kidney function (eGFR)?
2. Is there protein (albumin) in my urine?
3. What is my potassium level?
4. Given my medicines, are there foods I should limit?

CALL YOUR DOCTOR OR 911 IF YOU HAVE
Burning or urgency with fever. Pain in your back or side. Sudden confusion. A fluttering heartbeat with weakness. Fainting. Chest pain.


📚 RESEACH SOURCES:
1. CDC. Chronic Kidney Disease in the United States, 2023.
2. Johnson SA, et al. Daily blueberry consumption improves blood pressure and arterial stiffness in postmenopausal women with pre- and stage 1-hypertension. Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. 2015;115(3):369-377.
3. Williams G, et al. Cranberries for preventing urinary tract infections. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 2023;4:CD001321.
4. Pigeon WR, et al. Effects of a tart cherry juice beverage on the sleep of older adults with insomnia: a pilot study. Journal of Medicinal Food. 2010;13(3):579-583.
5. National Kidney Foundation. 40 Low Potassium Fruits and Vegetables to Add to Your Grocery List.
6. NIDDK / National Institutes of Health. Potassium: tips for people with chronic kidney disease.

DISCLAIMER
This video is for general education only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, and it does not replace a visit with your own doctor, pharmacist or kidney dietitian. If you have kidney disease, diabetes, heart disease, or take prescription medicines, talk to your care team before changing your diet or using any supplement, salt substitute or juice. No food or fruit can cure kidney disease. The people described in this video (Ruth, Gene, Harold, Evelyn and Linda) are fictional examples, and individual results will differ. Never ignore or delay medical care because of something you saw in a video.

If this helped you, please share it with someone over 60, and subscribe. It costs you nothing.


#kidneyhealth  #kidneyfailure  #healthyaging #seniorhealth
